name: thefirestore-experiment
description: Hand-authored registry modeled from observations of thefirestore.com (BigCommerce Stencil, firefighter gear e-commerce). Contrast target vs bungee-pro: no CSS custom property layer, raw-hex-only styling. See variant-rationale.md and FINDINGS.md for comparison.

components.name: Button
components.description: Primary CTA button. Four color variants declared in the stencil theme: primary (brand red), secondary (black), tertiary (ghost/white), accent (gold). Sizing variants (large, small, slab, icon) exist separately.

components.name: ProductCard
components.description: Product tile with image, caption overlay, and optional hover action. Two observable treatments: default (transparent card, figure bg white, gray border) and alternate (red hover border, red body on hover). Core e-commerce primitive.

components.name: CategoryTile
components.description: Category grid tile (Helmets, Boots, Gloves, etc.). Observable on homepage as a 16-tile grid. Image + category label + 'SHOP' link pattern.

bg.default.reason: GSS: body { background: #fff } in the stencil theme. Direct mapping — the one unambiguous case on this site.

text.primary.reason: GSS: body { color: #41423f } — the stencil theme uses a dark charcoal rather than pure black. Confidence dropped from bungee-pro's 0.95 because #41423f isn't a canonical 'black' hex; a value-based auto-mapper could plausibly bind it to text.muted instead of text.primary. The provenance (body selector) is what makes it primary.

text.muted.reason: GSS: Used on .card-text and similar secondary contexts. Medium-gray, clearly dimmer than body text. Confidence moderate because the site uses at least 8 distinct grays (#333, #41423f, #505050, #666, #757575, #8f8f8f, #909090, #999) and only one DCP text.muted slot — any automated mapping collapses most of these into one role, losing information.

accent.primary.reason: GSS: Brand fire-engine red, used on .button--primary default state, category CTAs, and most action surfaces. Highest-signal brand color on the site. The role binding is defensible but not automatic — #c12126 on its own gives a value-based mapper no reason to prefer accent.primary over intent.danger (it IS a danger-red hex). Provenance (appears on primary action buttons, not on error states) is what disambiguates.

intent.danger.reason: GSS: AMBIGUOUS: same hex as accent.primary. On most design systems, primary brand accent and error/danger signal are distinguished. On thefirestore — firefighter gear — the brand color IS danger-red by design. A human has to choose: (a) bind accent.primary, leave intent.danger unmapped, and note the collision; or (b) bind both roles to the same hex, accepting that the registry loses a semantic distinction the site itself has collapsed. Chose (b) with low confidence so the collision is visible in the registry rather than hidden.

accent.on.reason: GSS: Button primary and secondary variants both use color: #fff on top of colored backgrounds. Clean mapping to accent.on.

border.muted.reason: GSS: AMBIGUOUS: .card-image uses border: 1px solid #999. Could be border.default (the canonical 'neutral border' role) or border.muted (the dimmer variant). Picked border.muted because there's no lighter-toned border visible; #999 is effectively the site's only border treatment and it reads as dim, not structural. A value-based auto-mapper would likely bind this to border.default on lightness grounds alone — that would be a defensible different call.

--site-brand-red-hover.reason: Darker red, used as .button--primary:hover. Not a canonical DCP role — hover states aren't in the color contract. Stored as a themeContext extension. Bungee-pro did not produce any role-vocabulary-gap extensions; thefirestore produces one immediately because the site encodes interaction state (hover) in the palette itself.

--site-accent-gold.reason: Used on .button--accent. Warm gold, distinct from brand red. Could plausibly map to accent.primary (if you argue the site has two accent tones), but #c12126 is more broadly used, so this goes in extensions. Another judgment call where the DCP vocabulary is narrower than the site's expression.
